newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse rallies, but banking shares suffer.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse rallies, but banking shares suffer.

text.p: Norwegian shares raced to another all-time high on Wednesday stimulated by liquidity, a rally on major European bourses and falling interest rates, dealers said.
They said recent higher prices for oil and aluminium helped lift shares in industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro by almost four percent to 413 crowns.
Oslo's Total share index soared to a record close of 1,316.03 points the day after it smashed thorugh 1,300 points. The increase was 1.19 percent.
Turnover was heavy at 1.46 billion crowns.

Shares in Nera ASA jumped more than seven percent after the telecommunications company beat market expectations with its first-half profits. The share later fell back and closed unchanged at 49.50 crowns. It was the most traded share at 181 million crowns.
The banking index fell after Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse presented first-half profits that drew mixed reaction.
DnB shares closed 1.2 percent lower at 33.00 crowns and Christiania stock fell 3.2 percent to 27.60 crowns. Dealers spoke of a mix of profit-taking and disappointment.
